title: Kebra Nagast

translation.name: Kebra Nagast — E. A. Wallis Budge (14th c. (compilation); 1922 (translation))
translation.edition: The Queen of Sheba and Her Only Son Menyelek: A Complete Translation of the Kebra Nagast (London: Medici Society, 1922), from Bezold’s Ethiopic text

rightsNote: Budge (d. 1934); first edition 1922 — public domain in the US and the UK. (The 1932 OUP edition is not US public domain until 2028.)

canonicalStatus.ethiopianTewahedo: national epic and charter of the Solomonic dynasty; not Scripture

editorialMarkers: Budge’s 1922 translation from Bezold’s edition; chapter numbering follows Budge (117 chapters). OCR from a scan: ornamental opening initials at chapter starts are sometimes missing in the OCR and are left as scanned rather than guessed. OCR could not separate 9 chapter headings (11, 35, 36, 81, 92, 101, 110, 111, 112); their text is present within the preceding chapter — check the scan for exact boundaries.
citation: The Kebra Nagast, tr. E. A. Wallis Budge (Medici Society, 1922). Public domain; Internet Archive scan (item kebranagast).

provenance.method: OCR text of the scan, conservatively cleaned (hyphenation, running headers, page numbers). The scan’s own damage is repaired through scripts/ingest/repair.mjs: the translator’s footnotes and the publisher’s catalogue, which are not the author’s text; words split by the gutter; and letters the scanner misread where the printed word is not in doubt — a token no lexicon knows with exactly one candidate. Anything ambiguous is left as scanned, and every repair is counted in this record.
